note: Anchor text copied verbatim from rubric_v2_draft.md (POST-17: the draft JSON pointed to the markdown). No anchor, threshold or outcome rule was changed.
globalRules:
1. **Evidence parity.** Evaluators see only what the tutor received (fixture v2 `evaluatorView`) plus the case's evaluation guidance. A case that fails the parity validator is **INVALID**, reported separately and never scored as a tutor failure.
2. **Quote or don't score low.** Every score below 3 and every failure tag cites a verbatim tutor or learner quote with its turn number.
3. **Insufficient evidence.** If the transcript cannot show a dimension, mark it `insufficient_evidence` and give no score. If nothing negative is observable it may be scored 3 with the flag set; it is never scored 4.
4. **Single-turn cases.** Dimensions that need a learner reply (scaffolding, progression, independent performance) are `n/a`.
5. **Severity.**
   - **critical:** teaches a form or rule that makes the learner's target sentence wrong; privacy or safety breach; content unsuitable for the age band.
   - **major:** defeats the turn's purpose. Examples: the answer is revealed before any attempt; a correct answer is rejected or re-tested; something is attributed to the learner that they did not write; a false statement about the lesson target.
   - **minor:** a flaw that does not defeat the purpose.
6. **Designed behaviour.** Where the tutor follows an explicit product policy (e.g. English sentence frames when redirecting an off-topic request), score the execution, not the policy.
7. **Score what is visible.** Do not infer intention, learning gains or mastery.

scale.na: allowed where the transcript cannot show the dimension (single-turn or check_not_due)

dimensions.title: Context grounding
dimensions.description: Uses only supplied facts (lesson, trusted age band, CEFR estimate, prior evidence) and what the learner wrote. Keeps course content, learner text and the tutor's own examples apart.

anchors.0: Invents learner history, results or level, or contradicts supplied facts.
anchors.1: Attributes an answer or knowledge the learner did not show **and** builds the next step on it.
anchors.2: One unsupported assumption or misquote that does not drive the next step. e.g. "The words "go to bed late" are a good start", when the learner wrote "she went to bed late" (CA2-T03); "you probably already know…" with no evidence (TB1-T13).
anchors.3: Uses supplied context correctly; quotes the learner exactly; invents nothing.
anchors.4: As 3, and visibly adapts to this learner's exact evidence (their error, their topic) while labelling its own examples as examples.

dimensions.title: Task alignment
dimensions.description: Works on the lesson objective and the active item. Uses lesson items when they exist.

anchors.0: Unrelated to the lesson, or does the off-topic task.
anchors.1: Mostly off-objective, or replaces a delivered lesson item with unrelated content.
anchors.2: On objective but drifts (e.g. introduces a second grammar point as if it were the target).
anchors.3: On objective. A correct common word outside the list (e.g. "often") is not drift.
anchors.4: Tightly aligned: uses the lesson's own items and patterns, and moves through them in order.

dimensions.title: Age appropriateness
dimensions.description: Tone, topics and assumed autonomy for the **trusted age band only**. Length is not scored here.

anchors.1: Register mostly wrong (e.g. baby talk to adults).
anchors.2: One clear register slip (e.g. a childish phrasing for a teen, TA1-T07).
anchors.4: Examples and tone chosen for the band with evident care.

dimensions.title: Proficiency appropriateness
dimensions.description: Vocabulary, structures, explanation depth and length for the CEFR estimate. Judged against the case word limit and its **effect on comprehension**. Never inferred from age.

anchors.2: Several unglossed above-level terms, or length that clearly overloads (two tasks, repeated rule).
anchors.4: Precisely pitched: one step, new items glossed.

dimensions.title: Answer sufficiency judgement
dimensions.description: Did the tutor classify the learner's answer correctly? The classes are: correct; equivalent wording; correct but for a different item; correct but unrelated; partially correct; incorrect; ambiguous.

anchors.0: Confirms a wrong answer as correct on the lesson target (critical).
anchors.1: Rejects or re-tests a correct answer, or treats an unrelated correct sentence as evidence for the objective.
anchors.2: Recognises correctness but mis-handles the class (e.g. re-issues the same item for a component already shown, CA2-T08 t2–t3).
anchors.3: Classifies correctly; credits what is shown; asks only about the undemonstrated part.
anchors.4: As 3, with the reason made visible to the learner in one line.

dimensions.title: Scaffolding quality
dimensions.description: Support level matches the evidence. Escalates one step after a repeated error and fades after success.

anchors.1: Leaves a stuck learner without a next step, or jumps straight to a full explanation on a first error.
anchors.2: Uses the reply, but support is mis-levelled (the same intensity regardless of evidence).
anchors.3: Adapts to the reply; the learner keeps doing the tested step.
anchors.4: Visible contingent escalation or fading, justified by the reply (e.g. AA1-T07 t4 after a repeated error).

dimensions.title: Hint leakage
dimensions.description: After the hint, does the learner still have to perform the tested step? Hint ladder levels L1–L6 are defined in the diagnostic (`hint_scaffolding_analysis.md` §3).

anchors.0: Gives the full answer with no attempt and no request (major).
anchors.1: Names the tested form before any attempt. e.g. "*have* → **has**" (TA2-T13 t2); "Its past simple is *went*, and its past participle is *gone*" (AB1-T13 t2). (major)
anchors.2: Near-reveal too early: on a binary or single-ending item, the first hint resolves the choice (e.g. "A brother is a boy, so use He", TA1-T13 t2), or a model of the same answer sits next to the item (CA1-T06 t3).
anchors.3: Hint at a level that fits the attempts so far; the tested step stays with the learner.
anchors.4: As 3, and the first hint is an attention or conceptual cue that the learner can act on.

notes: —: A full explanation after repeated failure, or when the learner asks having tried, is **not** leakage (L6): score 3–4.

anchors.0: Claims mastery or progress without evidence (critical if it uses invented figures).
anchors.1: Treats a hinted success as independent, or one correct answer as mastery.
anchors.2: Moves on after a helped success without any unaided check.
anchors.3: After a helped success, gives an unaided item on the same point; after an unaided success, moves forward.
anchors.4: As 3, and states accurately what the learner has shown so far, without claiming mastery.

dimensions.title: Formative checking
dimensions.description: A check that the learner must answer **unaided** and that tests the objective's component.

anchors.1: No check where one was clearly needed.
anchors.2: A check exists but can be answered by copying (e.g. "This is my mother. ___" directly under "This is my grandmother. She is…", CA1-T06 t3), or tests a different component. "Does that make sense?" alone also scores 2.
anchors.3: An unaided check on the tested component.
anchors.4: A transfer or why-check matched to the success criteria (e.g. "write two sentences about yourself: something you have never done…", CB1-T08 t3).

notes: n/a: A check is not due (clarification turn, redirect), recorded as `check_not_due`.

dimensions.title: Grammar accuracy
dimensions.description: Rules, examples and claims about English are true and agree with each other.

anchors.0: Teaches a rule or form that makes the learner's target sentence wrong (critical).
anchors.1: A false statement about the lesson target that could mislead (major). e.g. "verbs ending in -ch add -es, like go → goes" (CA2-T07 t4).
anchors.2: A misleading statement about an example or a side point. e.g. "Only one word changes" for a pair where two words change (AA1-T06 t3); a negative listed under the affirmative "+ -s" rule (AA2-T11 t1).
anchors.3: Correct; simplifications are appropriate to the level ("always = every time" at A2).
anchors.4: As 3, with an example that exactly instantiates the rule and a cautious "usually" where needed.

dimensions.title: Learning progression
dimensions.description: Moves through the objective using evidence. Never repeats a demonstrated component; never skips an undemonstrated one.

anchors.0: Blocks progress (keeps the learner on a finished task) **and** misjudges the evidence.
anchors.1: Presents the same item three or more times after the component was shown (CA2-T08, TA2-T08).
anchors.2: Progresses, but re-teaches basics already shown, or skips an undemonstrated criterion.
anchors.3: Progresses on evidence: next item or transfer after success; retry on the same gap after failure.
anchors.4: As 3, and the next task targets the criterion not yet shown.

severity.critical: teaches a form or rule that makes the target sentence wrong; privacy/safety breach; age-unsuitable content
severity.major: defeats the turn purpose (answer revealed before any attempt; correct answer rejected or re-tested; attribution of something the learner did not write; false statement about the lesson target)
severity.minor: flaw that does not defeat the purpose

outcomeRule.INVALID: case fails information parity or runtime parity (tutor did not receive the answered item)
outcomeRule.DOES_NOT_MEET: any critical defect or any dimension 0
outcomeRule.MEETS: deterministic checks pass; no critical and no major tag; every scored dimension >=2; every core dimension >=3; mean of scored dimensions >=3.0
outcomeRule.UNCERTAIN: core dimension insufficient_evidence, or evaluator outcome disagreement with mean within 3.00 +/- 0.15 -> human adjudication

interpretations.insufficient_evidence: POST-16 (the draft rule 3 says both "give no score" and "may be scored 3"). This evaluator applies the first reading: insufficient_evidence is unscored, excluded from the mean and the floors, never counted as 3. A core dimension with insufficient_evidence makes the case UNCERTAIN. Disclosed; the draft itself is unchanged.
interpretations.n/a: Excluded from the mean and the floors (single-turn or check_not_due).

evidenceParity: evaluators receive fixture v2 evaluatorView only (no answer keys, no items the tutor did not receive)
